info.bio:
David Crosby inicia en los años 60 su andadura musical fundando The Byrds, grupo esencial en la música pop americana.  Después con Nash y Sitlls formará Crosby, Stills and Nash, grupo al que después se reincorpora Neil Young.  
Colaborador de lujo por sus armonías vocales de múltiples artistas, continua actualmente grabando y es considerado artista de culto.

scenes.name: The Byrds
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Su «Mr Tambourine Man» (1965), sin pretenderlo, fue el primer gran éxito de la cultura de la droga: la voz de McGuinn, mezcla de Lennon y Dylan, en un éxtasis pasivo sobre el dron hipnótico de la Rickenbacker de doce cuerdas. Tomaron LSD con Lennon y Harrison en agosto de 1965. «Eight Miles High» (14 de marzo de 1966), empezada por Gene Clark tras su viaje a Londres y forjada en una gira escuchando a Ravi Shankar y a John Coltrane (Impressions, Africa/Brass), fundía free jazz y música india, las dos bandas sonoras secretas de beats y hipsters, en un disco nuevo e irresistible de tensión y alivio. En la rueda de prensa del 28 de marzo, con un sitar sobre la mesa que no suena en el disco, nació el «raga rock»; Crosby habló demasiado del ácido. El Gavin Report la vetó como canción de drogas y se estancó en el número 14: fue la cima de su carrera.

scenes.name: Locura psicodélica y space-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El boom psicodélico y el desacondicionamiento hippy alumbran una generación de originales: Syd Barrett y sus dos obras maestras de folk psicodélico (Madcap Laughs, Barrett), Twink y los Pink Fairies, Peter Green (The End Of The Game), Hawkwind, inventores del space-rock entre la cultura hippy y el punk. En EE UU, Bruce Palmer, David Crosby (If I Could Only Remember My Name), Merrell Fankhauser y Mu, Ya Ho Wha 13. En Japón nace el space-rock con Hadaka no Rallizes, la Taj Mahal Travellers («La Monte Young con ácido»), Keiji Haino y Fushitsusha.

podcast.title: Backing Vocals on "Hold My Hand"
podcast.body: David Crosby provided backing vocals on the re-recording of Hootie & the Blowfish's song "Hold My Hand" for their *Cracked Rear View* album. This contribution by the legendary musician added a notable layer to the track, with the transcript noting "Rest in peace, Mr. Crosby." "For the re-recording of Hold My Hand, Atlantic managed to secure none other than David Crosby to provide backing vocals on the chorus."

podcast.title: Master of Harmonic Arrangement for CSNY
podcast.body: Recognized as a "musical genius," David Crosby was responsible for arranging most, if not all, of the intricate harmonies on Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young's album *Déjà Vu*. His pioneering harmonic arrangements were crucial in "plant[ing] the seeds for the soft rock boom to come." "he arranged most if not all of the harmonies on this record and in doing so he plants the seeds for the soft rock boom to come."

podcast.title: Orchestration of "Ohio" Recording
podcast.body: After Neil Young wrote "Ohio" in response to the Kent State shootings, David Crosby contacted Graham Nash to assemble the band in Los Angeles to record the song. Ahmet Ertegun, head of Atlantic Records, expedited its release, getting the record onto the streets within 10 days in a sleeve featuring the text of Article 1 of the First Amendment. "David Crosby called Graham Nash and the band assembled in Los Angeles and recorded the song Almit Erdogan, the head of Atlantic Records, took that record and within 10 days that record was on the streets in a sleeve with the text of Article 1 of the First Amendment."

podcast.title: Praise for Neil Young's "Ohio"
podcast.body: David Crosby considered Neil Young's decision to specifically name Richard Nixon in the song "Ohio" as the bravest act he had witnessed in music. Crosby was instrumental in the song's creation, having shown Young the Kent State photo spread in Life magazine, which immediately inspired Young to write the song. "David Crosby said it was the bravest thing he had seen in music."

podcast.title: Self-Description as "A Thorough Prick"
podcast.body: After being fired from The Byrds, David Crosby later described his past self as "a thorough prick," reflecting on his challenging personality. "he was fired from the birds and said later that he was quote a thorough prick."
